introduction: The Vault is where I keep the stuff that never really left.

These aren't necessarily the best games I've played, the best movies I've seen, or the greatest albums ever made. They're the things I keep coming back to. The stuff I replay, rewatch, relisten to, recommend to friends, and somehow end up thinking about years later.
Some entries have been here for years. Some might only stay for a few months before something else earns the space. That's part of the fun.
Nothing here is ranked. Nothing here is permanent.
It's just what's living on the shelf right now.
rotatingNote: Selections rotate. The shelf is never finished.

entries.title: Manhunt
entries.note: Every time someone brings up Manhunt, the conversation immediately goes to the controversy. I think that's a shame because what's always stuck with me is the atmosphere. The grime, the sound design, the feeling that the city itself wants you dead. It's one of Rockstar's most unapologetic games, and even two decades later there really isn't anything quite like it. Whether you enjoy it or not, it's an important piece of gaming history, and that's reason enough for it to have a place in my collection.

entries.title: Clock Tower 3
entries.note: There's something about Clock Tower 3 that I don't think any other horror game has managed to replicate. Everything about it feels operatic. The music swells at exactly the right moments, the villains chew every scene they're in, and the story unfolds with this larger-than-life sense of tragedy. It isn't trying to be grounded. It's putting on a performance, and I absolutely love it for that. Games this committed to their own identity deserve to be remembered.

entries.title: Sorority Babes in the Slimeball Bowl-O-Rama
entries.note: Every collection needs something that's just unapologetically fun, and this is mine. Sorority Babes in the Slimeball Bowl-O-Rama isn't trying to reinvent horror. It's here to throw a tiny demon, bowling alleys, goofy practical effects, and enough charm to make you wonder why movies don't get this weird anymore. It's impossible for me to watch without smiling, and I think cult horror is better because films like this exist.

entries.title: Oakland
entries.note: I don't think Oakland gets talked about nearly enough. Every time I throw it on, I'm reminded that heavy music isn't just about being the loudest band in the room. It's about having something that sticks with you. Suffokate found this filthy, pissed off sound that feels completely their own, and that's exactly why it's earned a permanent spot in my collection. It's rough around the edges, unapologetic, and memorable. I'd take that over polished and forgettable any day.
